newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
-- THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

United States State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns indicated yesterday the issue of a free trade agreement with Australia is likely to come up in talks between Prime Minister John Howard and United States president Bill Clinton in Washington next wee. However, there are signs from the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade that the proposal would be rejected, with a Cabinet paper arguing it would have little benefit for Australia's trade. At a meeting in Melbourne yesterday, corporate advisers working on the Telstra float advised the Telstra board to write down its cable investment by close to A$1 billion, as the investment represents a significant drain on future profits unless drastic an immediate action is taken. Page 37.

British company Cable & Wireless Group has consolidated its position in Optus Communications by yesterday appointing another two key executives to control the merger between Optus and its pay-TV offshoot Optus Vision. Cable & Wireless is also expected to buy out the other main foreign shareholder, Bell South. Page 37.

Goodman Fielder Ltd managing director David Hearn yesterday suggested the company may call on its shareholders to help pay for its international expansion. In comments that came as shares in the company rose to a near six-year high, Hearn said Goodman is beginning to have a shareholder confidence base. Page 38.

Woolworths Ltd group managing director Reg Clairs yesterday announced the appointment of Roger Corbett to the position of managing director, retail. Corbett's appointment follows the resignation of John Brunton from the role of managing director, supermakets, and will take effect on July 1. Page 38.

Simplot Australia, the local arm of United States-based food processor JR Simplot Co, will merge its seafood, snack and meal division with I&J Foods, an Australian division of South African based Irvine and Johnson Ltd. The deal will create a A$200 millin company which will hold a 70 per cent share of the frozen seafood retail market. Page 38.

THE AUSTRALIAN Pacific Dunlop is facing legal action on several fronts because of its heart pacemaker leads. A court action involving 9000 patients is being heard in California and covers allegedly faulty leads manufactured by its former subsidiary Telectronics Pacing ystems, while there is already another class action in the US over its Accufix J pacemaker lead, and the possibility of similar action in Canada and Australia. Page 19.

In a move that reinforces the strength of British telephone company Cable & Wireless within Optus Communications, new Optus chief executive Peter Howell-Davies, himself a former C&W executive, yesterday announced the appointment of two more executives fro C&W to assist the company as its faces the daunting task of integrating the loss-making Optus Vision pay-TV subsidiary into its own business. Page 19.

The 1997 Australian Stock Exchange shareholder survey released yesterday showed a 14-per cent increase in the number of Australians investing on the stock exchange, with most new investors buying stocks in secure companies such as BHP, WMC and the Commonwalth Bank. Page 19.

In a sweeping review of BHP's coal portfolio, joint partners in the Central Queensland Coal Associate - BHP Australia Coal, QCT Resources, Mitsubishi Development and AMP - will spend A$500 million to expand the Peak Downs and Saraji open-cut coking coal mnes in the Bowen Basin. Page 21.

Building materials giants Pioneer, Boral and CSR yesterday appeared in Brisbane's Federal Court to fight a class action against them by the Gold Coast City Council for damages relating to their involvement in a concrete price-fixing cartel. The companiesare moving to have the class action struck out on the grounds that the council's claims are "speculative", as the minimum requirement of seven complainants was not met. Page 21.

In changes that come as Woolworths moves into the A$18 billion "new age" prepared food market, managing director Reg Clairs has announced the appointment of Roger Corbett to managing director, retail, an appointment seen as confirming Corbett as the evental successor to Clairs. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After a slow start to the year, the Australian All Ordinaries sharemarket index was just shy of 2700 after another record finish yesterday of 2693.3, which added about A$45 billion to its overall value. The sharemarket has benefited from interest rate cus and confidence over Australia's resource stocks. Page 27.

In a move to reach its target of saving A$175 million in costs from its merger with the Advance Bank, the St George Bank will fast-track the integration of Advance by speeding up branch closures and staff reductions. St George has so far closed 20 branchs and retrenched their staff, while 200 staff have gone from the Bank's head office. Page 27.

Despite reports that the Telstra board would consider a proposal of a deal with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp involving the winding back of its cable roll-out, the deal is still some weeks away, with critical issues such as compensation and a distribution offunds still to be discussed. Page 27.

Following a review of BHP's world-wide coal operations which concluded the Bowen Basin coalfields were a worthwhile investment, BHP has announced it is planning to spend A$500 million expanding the Peak Downs and Saraji mines, and increasing port capacity Page 27.

Rob Jeffress, the managing director of Australia's largest media monitoring firm Media Monitors, has warned Australia's media monitoring industry could be put out of business and hand control to major publishers John Fairfax Holdings and News Ltd if changes to the Copyright Act introduced in Parliament on Wednesday go through. Page 29.

The Federal Court will continue hearing a matter between telecommunications service provider First Netcom and Telstra, with First Netcom seeking an injunction to prevent Telstra disconnecting it from the Telstra network for failing to pay a A$13 million dsputed bill. Page 29.
THE AGE

An Australian Stock Exchange Survey has found one third of Australia's adult population now own shares, and puts the increase down to compulsory superannuation, low inflation, a bull-run and a number of well known public floats. Around 4.7 million people now own shares, compared to around two million in 1991. Page B1.

Following a doubling of net profit to A$94.7 million for Rothmans Holdings, which holds almost a third of Australia's A$4 billion tobacco market, United States-owned Philip Morris Australia yesterday reported a lift in annual net profits to A$49.9 million The company's recoveries come after a decline in the number of smokers, a suicidal price war, and negative publicity. Page B1.

Air New Zealand has bought out Isi Leibler's half share in travel agency and technology business Jetset, lifting its stake to 100 per cent. The purchase is a turnaround for Air New Zealand, which had hoped to sell its 50 per cent share to Qantas, and sigifies an end to the airline's unhappy relationship with Leibler. Page B1.

Optus Communications yesterday announced new management appointments following the resignation of Ziggy Switkowski a week ago. Chief operating officer Phil Jacobs will take on an expanded role, while Britons Norman Gillespie and Christopher Weston, two rcruits from shareholder Cable & Wireless, were appointed finance director and strategy and regulation director respectively. Page B1.

A new report released today by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, The New Aseans: Vietnam, Burma, Cambodia, and Laos, indicates that while Vietnam is very poor now, in a generation it will be one of the economic giants of Asia. The report said economic growth in Vietnam was at 8 per cent. Page B3.

The Business Trends and Prospects Survey by the Victorian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which surveyed 350 of its members, has found Victorian business expects the State economy to grow faster than the national economy over the next year. The report lso showed uncertainty over the Federal Government's agenda left business confidence weak in a number of sectors. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
